STEP 2: the reflexive pronoun matches the subject. STEP 3: the preposition belongs to the German verb, not to English: wait FOR = warten AUF, think OF = denken AN, interested IN = interessiert FÜR, talk ABOUT = sprechen ÜBER.

O verbo reflexivo, passo a passo: The reflexive verb, step by step
PASSO 1: um verbo é REFLEXIVO quando a a: STEP 1: a verb is REFLEXIVE when the action goes back to the person doing it: «Ich wasche mich» (I wash myself). STEP 2: it uses a REFLEXIVE PRONOUN that repeats the subject: ich → mich, du → dich, er/sie/es → sich, wir → uns, ihr → euch, sie/Sie → sich. STEP 3: in the sentence, the pronoun comes right after the conjugated verb: «Ich freue mich.» If the sentence starts with something else: «Heute freue ich mich.» STEP 4: with a separable verb, the prefix goes to the end: «Ich ziehe mich an» (I get dressed). STEP 5: with a modal, the reflexive comes before the infinitive: «Ich muss mich beeilen» (I have to hurry). STEP 6: many German reflexive verbs are not reflexive in English at all: «sich freuen» (be glad), «sich treffen» (meet), «sich setzen» (sit down), «sich beeilen» (hurry). Learn each verb together with its «sich» — saying «Ich beeile» is like saying "I hurry myself" left half-finished.

Reflexivos com preposição e o reflexivo: Reflexive verbs with prepositions, and the dative reflexive
PASSO 1: muitos reflexivos pedem uma PRE: STEP 1: many reflexive verbs take a FIXED PREPOSITION that you learn together with the verb: «sich freuen auf» + accusative (look forward to something coming): «Ich freue mich auf den Urlaub»; «sich freuen über» + accusative (be happy about something you have): «Ich freue mich über das Geschenk»; «sich interessieren für» + accusative (be interested in); «sich erinnern an» + accusative (remember); «sich ärgern über» + accusative (be annoyed about). STEP 2: «sich entschuldigen» (apologize) takes «bei» + dative for the person and «für» + accusative for the reason. STEP 3: the DATIVE REFLEXIVE: if the sentence ALREADY HAS a direct object (accusative), the reflexive pronoun goes into the DATIVE: «Ich wasche mir die Hände» (I wash my hands), «Ich putze mir die Zähne» (I brush my teeth). Notice: German says "I wash to-me the hands", not "my hands". STEP 4: the dative reflexive forms: mir, dir, sich, uns, euch, sich (only ich and du change).

Os reflexivos na rotina e na conversa: Reflexive verbs in your routine and in conversation
PASSO 1: na rotina, o alemão usa muitos: STEP 1: in daily routines, German uses many reflexive verbs: sich waschen, sich duschen, sich anziehen, sich beeilen, sich ausruhen. STEP 2: when the action is RECIPROCAL, the pronouns «uns», «euch» and plural «sich» mean "each other": «Wir treffen uns» (we meet), «Sie sehen sich jeden Tag» (they see each other every day). STEP 3: questions: «Freust du dich auf das Wochenende?», «Wann treffen wir uns?» STEP 4: the reflexive pronoun has a fixed place: after the verb (or after the subject, if the subject comes after the verb): «Freut er sich?»

Sich auf etwas freuen significa estar co: «Sich auf etwas freuen» means looking forward to something that hasn't happened yet. With «ich», the reflexive is «mich», in the accusative: Ich freue mich auf das Wochenende.
Sich beeilen significa apressar-se. Com: «Sich beeilen» means to hurry. With «du», the accusative reflexive is «dich»: Du musst dich beeilen.
Com wir, o pronome é uns. Em Wir treffen: With «wir», the pronoun is «uns». In «Wir treffen uns um zehn Uhr», it is reciprocal: we'll meet each other at ten.
Sich für etwas interessieren significa i: «Sich für etwas interessieren» means to be interested in something. With «er», the reflexive is «sich»: Er interessiert sich für Musik.
Para esperar por alguém ou algo, usa-se: To wait for someone or something, use «warten auf» + accusative: Ich warte auf den Bus. The preposition is part of the verb — English "for" becomes «auf».
Pensar em alguém é an jemanden denken, c: To think of someone is «an jemanden denken», with the accusative: Ich denke an meine Oma. Use «an», not «auf» or «über».
Pergunte pelo objeto esperado usando a p: Ask about the thing being waited for, using the preposition of «warten auf»: ___ wartest du?
Para perguntar pelo complemento de warte: To ask about the object of «warten auf» when it's a thing, use «worauf»: Worauf wartest du? (What are you waiting for?) The r links «wo» to a preposition that starts with a vowel.

Para falar sobre um assunto, usa-se spre: To talk about a topic, use «sprechen über» + accusative: Wir sprechen über das Wochenende. «Über» introduces the topic of the conversation.

Complete com a preposição da expressão i: Complete with the preposition of the expression: dream of a vacation — Ich träume ___ einem Urlaub.

Complete com a preposição da expressão i: Complete with the preposition of the expression: be afraid of the dog — Ich habe Angst ___ dem Hund.
Angst vor + dativo significa medo de: Ic: «Angst vor» + dative means afraid of: Ich habe Angst vor dem Hund. «Dem Hund» is the object of «vor».
Substitua o complemento destacado por um: Replace the object with a da(r)- compound built with the same preposition: Ich warte auf den Bus. → Ich warte ___.
Darauf substitui auf den Bus nesta retom: «Darauf» replaces «auf den Bus» here (English: "I'm waiting for it"). It's built from da + r + auf; the r appears before a preposition starting with a vowel.

Daran retoma an das Konzert. Mantém-se a: «Daran» stands for «an das Konzert». Keep the preposition «an» of «denken an» and add «da» with the linking r.
Substitua o complemento destacado por um: Replace the object with a da(r)- compound built with the same preposition: Wir sprechen über das Projekt. → Wir sprechen ___.
Darüber retoma über das Projekt. Mantém-: «Darüber» stands for «über das Projekt». Keep «über», from «sprechen über», in the form da + r + über.
